title: mrexprSrcrefToLabel() crashes after Shiny's sourceUTF8() #line directive change
description:
## Problem

After [rstudio/shiny#4352](https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/pull/4352), any app using `metaReactive2()` (or `metaReactive()` inside a module) crashes when a session connects:

```
Error in while (!grepl("metaReactive", firstLine) & firstLineIdx >= 1) { :
  argument is of length zero
```

Stack trace:
```
56: mrexprSrcrefToLabel
55: exprToVarname
54: metaReactive2
53: server [app.R#7]
```

## Minimal Reprex

With `pak::pak("rstudio/shiny@v1.12.1.9000")` (or any commit at or after `9b78be110`):

```r
library(shiny)
library(shinymeta)

shinyApp(
  ui = fluidPage(textOutput("txt")),
  server = function(input, output, session) {
    dataset <- metaReactive2({
      metaExpr({ mtcars })
    })
    output$txt <- metaRender(renderText, {
      nrow(..(dataset()))
    })
  }
)
```

The app starts but crashes immediately when a browser connects and the server function runs.

## Root Cause

Shiny's `sourceUTF8()` now wraps app code with two extra lines **before** parsing:

```r
lines <- c(
  "..stacktraceon..({",
  sprintf('#line 1 "%s"', file),
  original_lines,
  "})"
)
src <- srcfilecopy(file, lines, isFile = TRUE)
exprs <- parse(text = lines, keep.source = FALSE, srcfile = src, encoding = enc)
```

The `#line 1` directive tells R's parser to remap line numbers back to the original file's numbering. This means:

- `srcref[1]` reports the **original** line number (e.g., line 4)
- But `srcfile$lines` contains the **wrapped** lines (with 2 extra lines prepended)
- So `srcfile$lines[srcref[1]]` is off by 2 — it hits the wrong line

### How this crashes `mrexprSrcrefToLabel()`

In [`R/utils.R` lines 68–109](https://github.com/rstudio/shinymeta/blob/v0.2.1/R/utils.R#L68-L109):

```r
firstLineIdx <- srcref[1]                                    # e.g. 4 (remapped)
firstLine <- substring(lines[firstLineIdx], 1, srcref[2] - 1) # lines[4] is wrong — 2 lines too early
while (!grepl("metaReactive", firstLine) & firstLineIdx >= 1) {
  firstLineIdx <- firstLineIdx - 1
  firstLine <- lines[firstLineIdx]  # walks backward past line 1...
}
```

The function starts at the wrong line (2 lines too early due to the offset), never finds `"metaReactive"`, walks backward past line 1 to `lines[0]`, which returns `character(0)`. Then `grepl("metaReactive", character(0))` returns `logical(0)`, crashing the `while` condition.

### Additional concern: `srcfilealias`

On the Shiny fix branch ([`fix/4357-renderplot-stack-fences`](https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/compare/main...fix/4357-renderplot-stack-fences)), the `#line` directive path is normalized while `srcfilecopy` keeps the original path. This causes R to create a `srcfilealias` object where `srcfile$lines` is `NULL` (the lines live in `srcfile$original$lines` instead). The current code at line 76–77 handles this by returning `defaultLabel`, but once the `srcfilealias` issue is fixed, the line-offset bug would still apply.

## Suggested Fix

The fix needs to address three things in `mrexprSrcrefToLabel()`:

### 1. Use the pre-remap line number from extended srcrefs

When a `#line` directive is present, R extends srcrefs to 8 elements. Element `[7]` is the **pre-remap** first line number — the actual position in the `srcfilecopy`'s lines. This is the correct index into `srcfile$lines`:

```r
line_num <- srcref[1]
if (length(srcref) >= 7 && srcref[7] != srcref[1]) {
  line_num <- srcref[7]
}
```

### 2. Handle `srcfilealias` objects

When `srcfile$lines` is `NULL`, fall back to `srcfile$original$lines`:

```r
lines <- srcfile$lines
if (is.null(lines) && inherits(srcfile, "srcfilealias")) {
  lines <- srcfile$original$lines
}
```

### 3. Fix the `while` loop guard

Prevent the crash when `firstLine` becomes `character(0)`:

```r
while (length(firstLine) > 0 && !grepl("metaReactive", firstLine) && firstLineIdx >= 1) {
```

### Reference

Shiny fixed the analogous issue in its own `rassignSrcrefToLabel()` and `rexprSrcrefToLabel()` functions via a `getSrcfileLines()` helper in commit [`df138b91e`](https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/commit/df138b91e). The same pattern should be applied here.

title: Is it possible to assemble the arguments for expandChain beforehand in a list?
description:
I'm currently developing a shiny app that has several steps. I'm looking to assemble all of these steps into a markdown/HTML report that the user can then download. Instead of a giant expandChain call at the very end of server.R, I'm looking to assemble this call piecemeal as a list of either expressions or expandChains, like this:

```r
code_chain <- list()
code_chain[[1]] <- expandChain(...)
# other code here
code_chain[[2]] <- expandChain(...)
# other code here
code_chain[[3]] <- expandChain(...)
# other code here
code_chain[[4]] <- expandChain(...)
# other code here
code_chain[[5]] <- expandChain(...)
# other code here
# Now combine it all somehow and render it as a single UI element
output$code <- renderText(code_chain)
```

or like this:
```r
code_chain <- list()
code_chain[[1]] <- substitute(...)
# other code here
code_chain[[2]] <- substitute(...)
# other code here
code_chain[[3]] <- substitute(...)
# other code here
code_chain[[4]] <- substitute(...)
# other code here
code_chain[[5]] <- substitute(...)
# other code here
# Now combine it all somehow and render it as a single UI element
output$code <- renderText(do.call(expandChain, lapply(code_chain, eval)))
```

Is this possible? I've tried several different manipulations of the above pseudocode with no success...

title: meta code for shiny::ExtendedTask()
description:
I have no success getting code within an extended task (i.e. `shiny::ExtendedTask()`) to become available via **shinymeta**. I imagine a `metaExtendedTask()` is missing to make this happen but, perhaps, I am over-complicating the problem. 

Is there a simple workaround that I am not aware of?
If not, is this on anyone's feature list? 

The code below is based on the `ExtendedTask` documentation with the output made meta-enabled. I think `metaAction` wrapped around the relevant code ( see "# Slow operation goes here" ) is the way forward, but not the complete answer. 

```
library(shiny)
library(shinymeta)
ui <- page_fluid(
  titlePanel("Extended Task Demo"),
  p(
    'Click the button below to perform a "calculation"',
    "that takes a while to perform."
  ),
  input_task_button("recalculate", "Recalculate"),
  p(textOutput("result"))
)

server <- function(input, output) {
  rand_task <- ExtendedTask$new(function() {
    future(
      {
        # Slow operation goes here
        Sys.sleep(2)
        sample(1:100, 1)
      },
      seed = TRUE
    )
  })

  # Make button state reflect task.
  # If using R >=4.1, you can do this instead:
  # rand_task <- ExtendedTask$new(...) |> bind_task_button("recalculate")
  bind_task_button(rand_task, "recalculate")

  observeEvent(input$recalculate, {
    # Invoke the extended in an observer
    rand_task$invoke()
  })

  output$result <- shinymeta:metaRender(
    shiny::renderText,
  {
    # React to updated results when the task completes
    number <- rand_task$result()
    paste0("Your number is ", number, ".")
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

title: How to call a metaObserve2 function inside expandChain()?
Can function contents be captured?
description:
Hi, I'm working on an app which contains a lot of code for making custom plots for which I am looking to export a reproducible script. Since the code is fairly complex, it is factored out into functions which are called by the `renderPlot()` function.

When I wrap the render call in `metaRender()` and the required `..()` calls, I get a script which calls the custom function, but that function is not captured anywhere. I am aware that this might be outside of the scope of this package, but is there any way to capture the custom function without moving the code back inside a render or reactive function?

I have considered making my custom functions into a package, but that doesn't quite address my use case of allowing users to make tweaks to the plots where adding more options is not practical.

Thanks
Janion

title: Don't formally import styler into NAMESPACE, but use `::`
description:
I am the author of the R package styler, which you use in your code. I repeatedly get strange and hard-to-reproduce reverse dependency errors when submitting a new version of my package to CRAN: Running `R CMD CHECK` on your package with a new version of {styler} results in problems like https://github.com/HenrikBengtsson/R.cache/issues/51 that I believe could be easily avoided by not importing {styler}. So instead of importing `style_text` into your `NAMESPACE` and use `style_file()` in your source code, you could use `styler::style_file()` in your source code and not import `style_text` into your `NAMESPACE`. I don't believe it would affect the user experience of your package.

Would you be open to that change? It has the potential to save me hours of debugging and stress. 😀

title: Move `master` branch to `main`
description:
Cc @schloerke

The `master` branch of this repository will soon be renamed to `main`, as part of a coordinated change across several GitHub organizations (including, but not limited to: [tidyverse](https://github.com/tidyverse), [r-lib](https://github.com/r-lib), [tidymodels](https://github.com/tidymodels), and [sol-eng](https://github.com/sol-eng)). We anticipate this will happen by the end of September 2021.

That will be preceded by a release of the [usethis package](https://usethis.r-lib.org), which will gain some functionality around detecting and adapting to a renamed default branch. There will also be a blog post at the time of this `master` --> `main` change.

The purpose of this issue is to:

* Help us firm up the list of targetted repositories
* Make sure all maintainers are aware of what's coming
* Give us an issue to close when the job is done
* Give us a place to put advice for collaborators re: how to adapt

title: is.reactive is FALSE for metaReactive variables
render functions that use installExprFunction() no longer work
description:
Ever since https://github.com/rstudio/shinymeta/commit/3a4b7e4959104d5fc130a369e7114d6a429e9d41, any render function that uses the old `installExprFunction()` approach instead of `quoToFunction()` is now broken. Since htmlwidgets doesn't yet use `quoToFunction()`, basically all widgets are broken, for example:

```r
library(shiny)
library(shinymeta)
library(DT)

ui <- fluidPage(
  dataTableOutput("p")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$p <- metaRender(renderDataTable, {
    datatable(mtcars)
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

```r
#> Error in <Anonymous>: 'data' must be 2-dimensional (e.g. data frame or matrix)
```

A handful of R packages are gonna need updating too before we could safely use `inject()` this way https://github.com/rstudio/shinymeta/commit/3a4b7e4959104d5fc130a369e7114d6a429e9d41#diff-0d68ae244e4a8c5ddc391c48f5399a91f18bc2a955f098e0e66069c607b444f4R79

title: Consider removing onload message

Managing complicated control flow
description:
Hello and thank you for your package.

In this example, what is the correct way to write the condition inside `metaRender` for a better display with the `Show code` button.
```r
library(shiny)
library(shinymeta)
library(ggplot2)

ui <- fluidPage(
  
  titlePanel("Old Faithful Geyser Data"),
  
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      sliderInput("bins",
                  "Number of bins:",
                  min = 1,
                  max = 50,
                  value = 30),
      radioButtons("column",
                   "Select column:",
                   choices = c("eruptions", "waiting"))
    ),
    
    mainPanel(
      outputCodeButton(plotOutput("plot"))
    )
  )
)

server <- function(input, output) {
  
  output$plot <- metaRender(renderPlot, {
    p <- ggplot(faithful, aes_string(..(input$column)))
    p <- p + geom_histogram(bins = ..(input$bins))
    if (..(input$bins<=30)) {
      p <- p + theme_dark()
    } else {
      p <- p + theme_bw()
    }
    p
  })
 
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

Here, the `Show code` button show :
```r
library(ggplot2)
p <- ggplot(faithful, aes_string("eruptions"))
p <- p + geom_histogram(bins = 30L)
if (TRUE) {
  p <- p + theme_dark()
} else {
  p <- p + theme_bw()
}
p
```
I would like it to simply display:
```r
library(ggplot2)
p <- ggplot(faithful, aes_string("eruptions"))
p <- p + geom_histogram(bins = 30)
p <- p + theme_dark()
p
```
Many thanks in advance for your support!

title: Print infix operators in a more familiar order
description:
In the example below, the code given by ```shinymeta``` works but it is different of what I expected. 
* Code expected: ```    mutate(!!lagged_name := lag(!!sym("mpg")))```
* Code obtained :  ```mutate(`:=`(!!lagged_name, lag(!!sym("mpg"))))```

Although the code obtained works, I'm worried it confuses the users when they try to see the code behind the shiny app. Is there a way to display infix operators in a more familiar way?

```
library(dplyr)
library(shiny)
library(shinymeta)

ui <- fluidPage(
  selectInput("choice", "Select a column", choices = c("mpg", "drat", "hp"), multiple = F),
  outputCodeButton(tableOutput("table"), label = "Show code")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  
  data1 <- metaReactive({
    data <- head(mtcars) 
    data$time <- rep(seq(1:3)) 
    data$ID <- rep(c("A", "B"), each = 3)
    data
  })
  
  data2 <- metaReactive({
    lagged_name <- paste0(..(input$choice), "_lagged")
    ..(data1()) %>%
      select(ID, time, sym(..(input$choice))) %>%
      group_by(ID) %>%
      mutate(!!lagged_name := lag(!!sym(..(input$choice))))
  })
  
  output$table <- metaRender(renderTable, {
    ..(data2())
  })
  
  observeEvent(input$table_output_code, {
    code <-  expandChain(data1(), data2())
    displayCodeModal(code)
  })   
  
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

Not sure at all if this is the right place to post this, sorry if it's not (also asked on [RStudio Community](https://community.rstudio.com/t/shinymeta-displays-a-strange-code-when-using-in-mutate/53118))

title: expandChain breaks when code contains a `parse()` statement
description:
Minimal example:

```
library(shinymeta)
input <- list(title = "paste(5, alpha)")
code <- metaExpr(parse(text = input$title))
expandChain(code)
```

Results in an error

```
Error: <text>:1:50: unexpected '<'
1: structure(expression(paste(5, alpha)), srcfile = <
                                                     ^
```

Example in a shiny app:

```
library(shiny)
library(ggplot2)
library(shinymeta)

ui <- fluidPage(
  textInput("text", "text", "paste(text, alpha)"),
  checkboxInput("parse", "Parse axis", FALSE),
  plotOutput("plot"),
  actionButton("code", "Show Code")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$plot <- metaRender2(renderPlot, {
    
    xtitle <- if (input$parse) parse(text = input$text) else input$text

    metaExpr({
      ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg,wt)) +
        geom_point() +
        xlab(..(xtitle))
    })
  })
  
  observeEvent(input$code, {
    code <- expandChain(output$plot())
    displayCodeModal(code)
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

title: Publish to CRAN so that we could use shinymeta in our packages
description:
I understand that shinymeta is likely considered in beta and may not be not very active development at the moment, but I still think it'd be useful to publish the current version to CRAN.

shinymeta in its current form does allow us to do things that that would otherwise be very difficult, and even with its current limitations it's still extremely helpful. But unfortunately using shinymeta means that we cannot submit our package to CRAN since shinymeta isn't on CRAN.

title: expandChain shouldn't require invokation of it's input
Escape quoted code that is a string
description:
(Forked from #73)

> (Hmmm, we might already have a bug here, if you put a {{placeholder}} in a code block and the value is a string I think it'll go into the Rmd verbatim rather than being deparsed.)

There's a fundamental quirk in R's code quoting, that quoted strings are represented as just strings.

```r
> identical(quote("foo"), "foo")
[1] TRUE
```

So if we use `knit_expand` to insert a code expr, and that code expr happens to be just a string, then the string will be inserted as _raw source code_, not a string literal.

````
```{r}
x <- {{x}}
```
````
```r
knit_expand(..., x = quote("Hello"))
```

results in

````
```{r}
x <- Hello
```
````

whereas what we want is

````
```{r}
x <- "Hello"
```
````

I think we can fix this by marking any just-a-string values with a special class, in the same place(s) as we add the `shinymetaExpr` class to calls. And then implementing `as.character`, `print`, `format`, `knit_print`, or whatever subset of those is necessary to ensure we always emit as a `deparse`d string.

title: Security footgun with Rmd generation
description:
The `{{` / `}}` `knit_expand` mechanism is a bit too low-level; since it works on a purely textual level, it's easy for values intended to be text to be interpreted as code instead.

e.g. an Rmd template that contains this snippet (not in a code block):

```
The variable we'll be focusing on in this report is {{col_name}}.
```

And then `buildRmdBundle(..., vars = list(col_name = input$col_name))`.

A malicious client could easily send a `col_name` value of `"\n```{r}\nunlink("whatever", recursive=TRUE)\n```\n"`, which would expand into the Rmd template as

    The variable we'll be focusing on in this report is 
    ```{r}
    unlink("whatever", recursive=TRUE)
    ```
    .

Some ideas:

* ~~We could add the values in `vars` to the knitr environment, then tell people to do `` `r col_name` `` instead of `{{col_name}}`.~~ (Won't work, see my next comment)
* ~~We could recommend people pass non-code values through `params`. That seems like a higher-overhead version of the previous option though.~~ (Won't work, see my next comment)
* We could error on suspicious `vars` or `{{`/`}}` substitutions. Yuck, security heuristics.
* We could stop using `knit_expand` altogether, and use a different chunk type to insert code dynamically. This would probably be a considerable amount of knitr hacking, I think I looked at this last time and I couldn't find an obvious way to preprocess a chunk and then have knitr treat it as code.

title: metaExpr introduces a local scope
description:
```r
> exists("foo")
[1] FALSE
> shinymeta::metaExpr({foo <- TRUE})
[1] TRUE
> exists("foo")
[1] FALSE
```

I think this is due to the use of `rlang::eval_tidy`:

```r
> rlang::eval_tidy(quote(foo <- TRUE))
[1] TRUE
> exists("foo")
[1] FALSE
```

Switching to `base::eval` will fix this.

title: Error in FUN: argument "x" is missing
description:
A minimal example:

```r
library(shiny)
library(shinymeta)

ui <- fluidPage(verbatimTextOutput("foo"))

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  mtc <- metaReactive({
    mtcars[1:5, ]
  })
  observe({
    print(expandChain(mtc()))
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

```r
Error in FUN(X[[i]], ...) : argument "x" is missing, with no default
```


The root cause is that `walk_ast()` will apply `fun` to each node of the AST, even if that node is a missing symbol:

```r
walk_ast(quote(mtcars[1:5, ]), identity)
```

```r
Error in FUN(X[[i]], ...) : argument "x" is missing, with no default
```

I think the solution is to have `walk_ast()` return `x` is it's a missing symbol before applying `fun`.

title: Customization of render functionality in bundles
description:
First I am so excited for this package and huge thanks for the shoutouts in the UserR presentation!  

I'm just beginning to play with this but had a thought about how the bundles could be processed.  For majority of use cases I agree that R Markdown reports are the optimal way to go.  But I do have some apps at the `$day_job` where the artifact I would like the user to produce from a bundle would be outside of R-Markdown (for instance a powerpoint slide or document produced by [`officer`](https://davidgohel.github.io/officer/)).  It may be outside of your scope but it would be nice to give users an option to specify how they want the R script to process the "artifact" of the code.  I realize after typing this I could just put all of the processing code inside a massive `quote()` call within the app so the user can just run it and have the desired output object produced, so perhaps that is the way to go in these cases.

title: Figure out a strategy for producing code that is a function of multiple objects
description:
Although probably fairly rare, I imagine in some cases, you might want to do something to output(s) to make them more presentable outside of shiny. Say, for example, this app I made (pre-`expandChain()`) which puts multiple outputs into a `gridExtra::grid.arrange()`:

```r
library(shiny)
library(shinymeta)
library(ggplot2)
ui <- fluidPage(
  plotOutput("p1"),
  plotOutput("p2"),
  actionButton("code", "R code", icon("code"))
)
server <- function(input, output) {
  output$p1 <- metaRender(renderPlot, {
    qplot(data = diamonds, x = carat) + ylab("Number of diamonds")
  })
  output$p2 <- metaRender(renderPlot, {
    qplot(data = diamonds, x = price) + ylab("Number of diamonds")
  })
  observeEvent(input$code, {
    code <- expandCode({
      library(ggplot2)
      gridExtra::grid.arrange(
        !!output$p1(),
        !!output$p2()
      )
    })
    displayCodeModal(
      code, 
      title = "ggplot2 code",
      size = "s", 
      fontSize = 16, 
      height = "200px",
      theme = "solarized_dark"
    )
  })
}
shinyApp(ui, server)
```

I suppose this could be an argument for keeping `expandCode()`, unless we can come up with a decent way to support this sort of thing with `expandChain()`. A decent workaround might be to provide a way to assign outputs to a name, then allow for referencing those objects in downstream quoted in expressions, so something like:

```r
expandChain(
  p1 = output$p1(),
  p2 = output$p2(),
  quote(gridExtra::grid.arrange(p1, p2))
)
```

would produce

```r
p1 <- qplot(data = diamonds, x = carat) + ylab("Number of diamonds")
p2 <- qplot(data = diamonds, x = price) + ylab("Number of diamonds")
gridExtra::grid.arrange(p1, p2)
```

title: Document some common mistakes/misunterstandings
Localize expressions?
description:
Suppose you have a reactive expression(s) that contain intermediate computations that you need, but don't: (1) want to extract those intermediate steps in their own reactives and (2) care about the objects created during these intermediate calculations. 

Currently you'd get something like this:

```r
options(shiny.suppressMissingContextError = TRUE)

mr <- metaReactive({
  a <- 1+1
  b <- a+1
  b+1
})

expandCode({mr <- !!mr()})
```

```r
mr <- {
  a <- 1 + 1
  b <- a + 1
  b + 1
}
```

Besides the fact that this isn't very readable, it also introduces objects into scope that you probably didn't intend too. Perhaps we could have an `local = TRUE` option (and have it be the default)?

```r
expandCode({mr <- !!mr()}, local = TRUE)
```

```r
mr <- local({
  a <- 1 + 1
  b <- a + 1
  b + 1
})
```

This last part is a bit off-topic, but it'd also be cool if we had a way to get back code like this:

```r
a <- 1 + 1
b <- a + 1
mr <- b + 1
```

title: Explore alternatives to patchCalls
description:
`expandCode()`'s `patchCalls` argument is hard to use because it requires knowledge of names used in the body of the meta expressions. Perhaps we could supply these names when initializing the meta objects, like

```r
filtered <- metaReactive(metaName = "top",
    !!df() %>% head(!!input$n)
  )
```

Then, in `expandCode()`, if other meta expressions reference `filtered`, they'd use the name `top` instead. This has the additional problem `top <- !!filtered()` would need to appear before any relevant downstream calculations, but maybe we auto-assign a call `!!filtered()` to the name `top` inside of `expandCode()`
